sections.content:
62,755 people

were counted on the census as "IT operations technicians" in England and Wales in March 2021.

IT operations technicians are responsible for the day-to-day running of IT systems and networks including the preparation of back-up systems, and for performing regular checks to ensure the smooth functioning of such systems.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "IT operations technicians" there were more men than women (80.4% compared with 19.6%).

This means "IT operations technicians" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "science, engineering and technology associate professionals".

Men made up 80.4% and women made up 19.6% of "IT operations technicians"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "IT operations technicians" included:

  • managers in storage and warehousing
  • elementary storage occupations (other)
  • production managers and directors in mining and energy

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "IT operations technicians", 14.7% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "IT operations technicians" was 65 years or older.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "IT operations technicians" included:

  • IT user support technicians
  • security system installers and repairers
  • chefs

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "IT operations technicians" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "IT operations technicians" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "IT operations technicians", 9.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (87.9% compared with 12.1%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (93%) than self-employed (7%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
